sources: Esri World Imagery z18 with the catalog site coordinates

values.note: Parking spurs 20-40 ft (FS). The recreation.gov catalog lists 33 sites: 25 take RVs, 8 tent-only. Most RV spurs are catalogued at 14-22 ft; nine take 26 ft or more (001, 004-007, 031 at 30; 022, 035 at 26; 034 at 35). 006 and 007 are pull-throughs. One RV or two vehicles per site.

sites.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r02/psicc/recreation/lodgepole-campground ('34 campsites with parking spurs 20-40 feet and a maximum trailer length of 30 feet'; 'The max length for RVs/trailers is 30 feet') + recreation.gov catalog 232301 (Max Vehicle Length, Driveway Entry), read 2026-10-28

hookups.source: recreation.gov 232301 notice 'No RV hookups are available' + catalog (all sites NONELECTRIC), read 2026-10-28

values.note: Water from a hand pump. Trash collection; picnic table, fire ring and pedestal grill at each site. Firewood $10 a bundle at the host site. Services may be limited early and late in the season.

facilities.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r02/psicc/recreation/lodgepole-campground ('Vault toilet(s)'; 'Potable water is available at this site. A hand pump is available.'; 'toilets, tables, water, trash and fire rings'; 'All services may not be available early or late in the season') + recreation.gov notice ('Firewood is available for sale at host site for $10.00/bundle'), read 2026-10-28

values.note: Mid-May to mid-October, weather dependent. Roads not plowed in winter.

season.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r02/psicc/recreation/lodgepole-campground ('This campground is open mid-May to mid-October, weather dependent'; 'The roads to this site are not maintained for snow throughout the winter'), read 2026-10-28

values.note: Book at least four days ahead. Friday and Saturday nights together on weekends, three nights on holiday weekends; walk-ups are exempt from the minimums. An unreserved site taken first-come must be occupied the same night, paid at the self-service fee tube.

booking.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r02/psicc/recreation/lodgepole-campground ('at least four days in advance. A minimum stay on Friday and Saturday night is required on weekends. A three-night minimum stay is required on holiday weekends. Walk-ups are exempt'; 'No more than a 14-night consecutive stay'; 'First-come, first-served sites must be occupied the same night') + https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/232301 (rules reservationCutOff 4, minWeekendStay 2) + /rates (2026 Peak 05-15 to 10-11), read 2026-10-28

values.note: Plus a one-time $11 Jefferson Lake Recreation Area entry fee per stay (annual pass available). A third vehicle is $11 a night.

fees.source: https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/232301/rates (2026-2028 Peak STANDARD NONELECTRIC 24) + notices ('one-time fee of $11.00 to enter Jefferson Lake Recreation Area'; '$11.00/night for a third vehicle'), read 2026-10-28

note: Largest of the Jefferson Lake Recreation Area campgrounds, at ~9,900 ft in aspen and mixed conifer in the Jefferson Creek valley, 4 miles north of Jefferson off CR 35 and CR 37, 3 miles below Jefferson Lake. Colorado Trail access. Campers report CR 37 as graded dirt, bumpy but passable for cars and RVs, and tight maneuvering for larger rigs. --Claude
summary: FS page + recreation.gov: confirmed 34 sites, max 30 (FS), no hookups, vault toilets, potable water (hand pump), reservable, $24 (2026-2028). Added pull-through, season note, booking.season 05-15..10-11, 14-night max, 4-day cutoff, 2-night weekend / 3-night holiday minimums, the $11 rec-area entry fee in fees.note. Note trimmed of field facts.
flags: Missing phone: South Park Ranger District 719-836-2031 (FS page contact block). recreation.gov's (661) 702-1420 is the concessionaire's.
Operator: concessionaire-run (recreation.gov contact tbolton@goexplorus.com, ExplorUS; FS page refers to 'concessionaire-run campsites'). Ownership federal stands.
Fee conflict: FS page says '$22 fee per site' (last updated February 3, 2026) vs recreation.gov $24 for 2026-2028. Recorded 24.

Short spurs: only nine of 25 RV sites are catalogued at 26 ft or more; most spurs are 14-22 ft. The 30-ft limit is the FS figure ('maximum trailer length of 30 feet'), above 23 ft, so no criteria issue.
Site count: FS 34 vs recreation.gov catalog 33. Kept 34.

Road: neither FS nor recreation.gov carries RV or 4WD wording for CR 35/37; the only agency road note is that the roads are not maintained for snow in winter. The 'graded dirt, bumpy' and 'tight maneuvering' text is camper-reported, kept in the note as such.

Waterfront (stored not waterfront) stands: recreation.gov calls it 'a creekside destination' and 'in a valley along Jefferson Creek', but on imagery the creek runs through willow meadow north-east of CR 37, ~100 m+ from the nearest site (001) with the county road between.
Pin 39.42243,-105.84187 (= the FS coordinate) is 76 m from the catalog site centroid. OK.
